hypothesis: Jerome's message ansatz (docs/JEROME_CALL_2026-09-25.md Q2/Q3/Q4): is a BP message of the form 'a Gaussian pushed through one transition of the true chain' -- what he called 'Gaussian plus the family of epsilon' -- exact when the innovation is that same family? Derived before measuring: NO. The recursion is L_{i+1} = dilate_rho(L_i * ell_i) conv p_eps, and (G conv p_eps) * N is not of the form (Gaussian conv p_eps), so the family is not closed. It IS exact in two limits: at site 1, where L_1 is the Gaussian prior pushed through one transition by construction, and as t grows and the likelihood flattens.
design: Forward messages of grid BP at (N_g = 801, A = 12), rho = 0.85, L = 32, 64 chains per cell, four innovation families (laplace, gaussian control, student, uniform) x the twelve frozen levels, read at sites (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31). Each message is fitted by direct Nelder-Mead minimisation of KL(true || candidate) over the candidate's own parameters -- every family given its best shot rather than a moment match -- for three candidates: gaussian (2 params), gauss_through_transition (2 params; Jerome's ansatz, built with the recursion's OWN kernel matrix so the quadrature matches exactly), gauss_plus_laplace (4 params). Part `cumulants` reports standardised kappa_3..kappa_6 of the same messages against t and site, the representation-independent form of the question and the direct input to E23's truncation order. Frozen confirmatory run E22c (amendment_2026_09_25; job 669837, cnode06, commit bd7ad42, 1 BLAS thread): 512 chains per cell, rho in {0.5, 0.85, 0.95}, L in {32, 128}, grids (801, 12) and (1601, 16), sites 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 31 and, at L = 128, 63 and 127. The 64-chain single-configuration laptop run (outputs/E22) is not frozen.
predeclared_analysis: P1 gauss_through_transition divergence at site 1 sits at the numerical floor. P2 it GROWS with site index into the interior: the family is not a fixed point. P3 it is non-monotone in t. P4 a plain Gaussian is uniformly worse at small t and converges to it as t grows. P5 message excess kurtosis decays with t, setting E23's mode budget. The floor is MEASURED, not assumed: the Gaussian-innovation family is the control, where all three candidates contain the true message exactly, so its KL at the same (level, site, ansatz) is pure quadrature. A failure of P2 -- divergence flat in site index at the control level -- would mean the ansatz IS closed and the grid could be replaced by four numbers; that is the better outcome, which is why the prediction is recorded in advance.

seeds.confirmatory: deterministic per cell: rng_for('e22-shapes', family, level), 64 chains

motivation: Jerome asked this three separate ways in one call and it had never been looked at: 'if you look at the messages mu_K, what do they look like?'; 'what if you take a Laplace ansatz for the messages in the BP -- is this exact when the innovation is exact? To me it's not immediate that they match'; 'I wonder if it's not Gaussian plus the family of epsilon'. It is the cheapest open question on the list and it decides two things at once: whether the real-space grid can be replaced by a handful of parameters, and how many modes a truncated representation needs at each level (E23).
development_note: The first implementation built the ansatz with a p_eps(u_i - u_j) lookup matrix applied to an already-dilated Gaussian, and measured 5.9e-8 nats at site 1 where the ansatz is analytically exact. That residual was the gap between two discretisations of the same convolution -- BP evaluates p_eps at the off-grid points u_i - rho u_j with the dilation folded into the kernel, a grid lookup cannot -- and reported as-is it would have looked like a small failure of the ansatz rather than a failure of the comparison. Rebuilding the candidate on the recursion's own kernel matrix takes the same site-1 fit to 3.8e-17, which is what makes P1 a usable control.

outcome.Q3: Jerome's conjecture is very nearly right. Frozen E22c, deepest site (31) at rho = 0.85, L = 32, grid 801, t = 0.05: the two-parameter 'Gaussian pushed through one transition' family has KL 1.56e-5 (Laplace) and 1.78e-6 (Student-t), against 3.54e-2 and 2.93e-2 for a plain Gaussian (2,272x and 16,464x) and 1.22e-3 and 4.97e-4 for the FOUR-parameter Gaussian+Laplace mixture (78x and 280x). Over the interior sites 2-31 of the same configuration the mixture-to-ansatz ratio is 73-101 (Laplace), 258-428 (Student-t) and 92-117 (uniform). At t = 0.05 the right two-parameter family beats a wrong four-parameter family by a factor of 73 to 428. The advantage shrinks as t grows and reverses at large t: at site 31 the mixture-to-ansatz ratio is 0.73 (Laplace) and 0.34 (Student-t) at t = 3, and the mixture is better in 296 of the 2,592 non-Gaussian interior cells of E22c. (The 1600x, 16000x and 50x first written here came from the unfrozen 64-chain laptop run outputs/E22, site 31: 1643x, 16394x and 57x.)
outcome.Q2: Not exact. Frozen E22c, 432 non-Gaussian cells (3 noise families x 3 rho x 2 lengths x 2 grids x 12 levels). P1: the site-1 KL is 5.8e-17 to 4.8e-14, machine precision, as derived, since L_1 is the Gaussian prior pushed through exactly one transition. The script's floor test (site-1 KL below 10x the Gaussian control's KL in the same cell) passes in 416/432 cells; the 16 failures are uniform noise at rho = 0.5, t <= 0.1527, where the site-1 KL is 2.4e-15 to 4.3e-15 against a control of 3e-17 to 4e-16: above the test's 10x line but still machine precision, so P1 stands in substance. P2 holds in 432/432 cells: the deepest-site KL is above the floor and grows with depth, by a factor of 6.7e7 to 3.3e11 (median 1.4e10) from site 1 to the deepest site (31, or 127 at L = 128), for all three non-Gaussian families and all twelve levels. Doubling the grid (801 -> 1601) leaves the ansatz KL unchanged (median ratio 0.9999 over 1512 cells), so the failure is the family, not the quadrature. The family is not a fixed point of the recursion. (The unfrozen laptop run outputs/E22 quoted here before gave site-1 KL 2.5e-15 to 3.1e-14 and growth of about 10^10 to site 31, with P1 and P2 in 36/36 cells.)
outcome.Q4: Exact closure is Gaussian-only (site 1 against the deepest site is the demonstration). Projected closure is available for any family at a price now measured rather than asserted: for the best two-parameter family the deepest-site KL is 1.8e-6 to 8.8e-4 nats per message at rho = 0.85, L = 32, grid 801, and 4.3e-9 to 2.0e-3 (median 2.3e-4) across all 432 frozen E22c cells. (This replaces '1e-5 to 1e-3', a rough summary of the unfrozen laptop run that missed Student-t at small t; that run itself gives 1.8e-6 to 8.8e-4 at this configuration.)
outcome.P3_falsified: Predicted the ansatz error would be SMALLEST at large t, because the likelihood flattens and the product step stops acting. Measured the opposite: in frozen E22c at rho = 0.85, L = 32, grid 801, deepest site (31), the error grows monotonically with t for Laplace and Student-t (1.6e-5 -> 7.7e-4; 1.8e-6 -> 8.8e-4); only uniform is non-monotone (5.6e-4 at t = 0.1527, 3.2e-4 at t = 3). Over the 36 (family, rho, L, grid) configurations of the frozen sweep the deepest-site error rises monotonically with t in 20, is non-monotone in 12 (Laplace at rho = 0.95, peaking at t = 0.47-0.98 and easing to 2.7e-4 at t = 3; uniform at rho = 0.5 and 0.85) and falls monotonically in 4 (uniform at rho = 0.95, 3.4e-4-3.6e-4 -> 5.6e-5-5.9e-5). For uniform noise at rho = 0.85 the error is also smallest at large t: the minimum is 3.0e-4-3.1e-4 at t = 1.425, against 3.5e-4-3.75e-4 at t = 0.05. So for uniform noise at rho >= 0.85 the error is smallest at large t. At t = 3 it is 5.6e-5 to 1.9e-3 in every configuration, far above the machine-precision site-1 values, so the ansatz is nowhere close to exact at the largest t measured. For Laplace and Student-t the prediction had the large-t limit backwards. With the likelihood flat the recursion is a pure repeated convolution, which drives the message to the chain's STATIONARY law -- an infinite convolution, maximally far from 'one Gaussian through one transition'. At small t the likelihood is sharp, L_i*ell_i is nearly a point mass, and the next message is nearly p_eps shifted, which is exactly in the family. The ansatz is best where the data is most informative. (The unfrozen laptop run outputs/E22 gave 2.2e-5 -> 7.7e-4 for Laplace.)
outcome.mode_budget_for_E23: Odd cumulants are small next to the even ones (symmetric noise): in frozen E22c at rho = 0.85, L = 32, grid 801 the per-message |kappa_3| has median 0.02 (at most 0.06), and |kappa_5| median 0.007-0.009 for Laplace and uniform noise but 0.25 for Student-t (at most 0.72), against |kappa_6| of at least 8 for Student-t; so a truncation can carry even orders only. Order 4 is NOT enough: at that configuration |kappa_6| runs from 0.15 (uniform, site 1, large t) to 229 (Student-t), at least 0.64 for Laplace and 8.0 for Student-t, so the Gaussian-plus-kappa_4 rung that e16_edgeworth_oracle builds will miss a large term; E23 must reach order 6 at least, more for heavy tails. Across all frozen E22c cells |kappa_6| is not uniformly large: it falls to 0.011 (0.0064 at site 1) for uniform noise at rho = 0.95, t = 3, and reaches 343 for Student-t. |kappa_4| decays with t but PLATEAUS (2.12 -> 0.48 for Laplace, site 31) because the message tends to the stationary law rather than to a Gaussian, so a t-adaptive truncation saves less than one might hope.
